instruction.text: Listen to Lauren’s thoughts about today’s football training, then answer the questions.

atoms.b: Why did I do that? I should have passed the ball earlier, and then we might have won.
I never get it right, and all my teammates think I’m bad. I don’t know why I play football.
I feel like I am never going to get better.

instruction.text: Answer the questions by selecting the correct button.

atoms.a: Does Lauren sound like she thinks she can improve?

feedback.end: Lauren is thinking that she will never improve and that she’s not very good.

atoms.a: Are her thoughts very kind to herself?

feedback.end: These aren’t very kind thoughts. You would never say these things to a friend.

atoms.a: Do you think she might feel even worse after thinking these thoughts than when she made the mistake?

feedback.end: Lauren is making the situation even worse than it has to be by thinking so unkindly about herself.

instruction.text: Let’s listen to an alternative conversation Lauren might be having with herself.

atoms.b: We were so close to winning! If I had just passed the ball sooner, we might have had them. That means we have a really good chance next week!
I wish I had done better at the end, but I made good plays earlier, and my defence was really good.
My teammates don’t mind when I make mistakes. We all make them! That’s just how we learn.
I am really proud that I keep trying to get better.

instruction.text: Answer the questions by selecting the correct button.

atoms.a: Does Lauren sound like she thinks she can improve?

feedback.end: Lauren knows that making mistakes is part of learning. Sometimes, you learn the most by making lots of mistakes.

atoms.a: Are her thoughts kind to herself?

feedback.end: If Lauren had a friend tell her about a mistake she made, she would have told her friend the same thing she was thinking!

atoms.a: Do you think she might feel even worse after thinking these thoughts than when she made the mistake?

feedback.end: Lauren will likely feel better after thinking these thoughts. She knows that she played well and that one little mistake does not mean that she is bad or will never improve. She’s even more excited for next week’s training.

instruction.text: Is this positive self talk? Decide quickly!

atoms.a: I am going to stay focused and calm and give it my best effort.
This is all my fault and everyone hates me.
I have stuck with things before, so I am not giving up this time.
It hurts when people say mean things, but I don’t have to believe what they say.
It’s pointless, I should just give up.
Even if my score wasn’t the best, I know I tried hard.

feedback.finish: Everyone faces challenges and stressful situations in life. Learning positive self-talk is important so that you can deal with these situations in a way that makes them better and not worse. Be kind to yourself!
